claims.claim: Severian of Gabala was Bishop of Gabala in Syria.
Severian flourished from around 400 until 404 as a popular preacher in Constantinople.
Severian was born in Syria and spoke Greek with a Syriac accent.
Severian became the enemy of John Chrysostom and helped condemn him at the Synod of the Oak.
Almost all of Severian's homilies survive only among the works of his enemy Chrysostom.
The work De tribus pueris was formerly attributed to John Chrysostom.
There are two CPG identifiers for De tribus pueris because manuscripts have been written under the name of either John Chrysostom or Severian of Gabala.
The CPG numbers for De tribus pueris are 4236a.3 and 4568.
The BHG number for De tribus pueris is 0488f.
